keywords.def: able to recover quickly from very difficult conditions
the division of a country’s territory among foreign powers
a rebellion or revolt against a ruling authority
a military operation in which forces surround a city to cut it off and force it to surrender
an extremely cruel or shocking act, especially one committed during wartime
the process of rebuilding something after destruction
a government in power, often with the suggestion of authoritarian control

sentences.en: Today, we’re going to talk about Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来聊聊华沙。

sentences.en: Warsaw is the capital of Poland and one of Europe’s most resilient cities.
sentences.zh: 华沙是波兰的首都，也是欧洲最有韧性的城市之一。

sentences.en: If you visit Warsaw today, you’ll find a modern and quickly developing European capital.
sentences.zh: 如果你今天去华沙，你会发现一个现代且发展迅速的欧洲首都。

sentences.en: There are skyscrapers, busy shopping streets, trendy cafés, and a growing economy.
sentences.zh: 那里有摩天大楼、繁忙的商业街、时尚的咖啡馆，经济也在不断增长。

sentences.en: But history of city is dramatic and tragic.
sentences.zh: 但这座城市的历史却充满戏剧性与悲剧色彩。

sentences.en: In this episode, I am going to explore the fascinating history of Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我将带大家探索华沙迷人的历史。

sentences.en: We’ll look at its rise as Poland’s capital, periods of foreign occupation and division, the devastation of World War II, communist rebuilding, and the modern city we see today.
sentences.zh: 我们将了解它作为波兰首都的崛起、历经外敌占领与瓜分、第二次世界大战的毁灭、共产主义时期的重建，以及我们今天所看到的现代城市。

sentences.en: And we will learn some new vocabulary and practice our English listening comprehension at the same time!
sentences.zh: 同时，我们还将学习一些新词汇，并练习英语听力理解！

sentences.en: Warsaw wasn’t always a capital city. Actually, before we get into the main part of the episode, I should probably mention that I’m going to use the British English pronunciation for most of these Polish place names.
sentences.zh: 华沙并非自古以来就是首都。其实，在进入正题之前，我可能得提一下，对于这些波兰地名，我大部分会使用英式英语的发音。

sentences.en: Polish and English are very different languages, so the pronunciations can be quite different.
sentences.zh: 波兰语和英语是截然不同的语言，所以发音可能会有很大差异。

sentences.en: And I’m also not using the American English pronunciations, but the British pronunciations.
sentences.zh: 而且我用的也不是美式英语发音，而是英式发音。

sentences.en: So I will be saying Warsaw to refer to the capital of Poland.
sentences.zh: 因此，我会把波兰首都读作 Warsaw。

sentences.en: But for a long time, Warsaw was just a modest community of fishermen and traders living behind the Vistula River.
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，华沙只是维斯瓦河畔一个简朴的渔民和商人社区。

sentences.en: The Vistula River is the longest river in Poland.
sentences.zh: 维斯瓦河是波兰最长的河流。

sentences.en: The community was in a strategic position between Eastern and Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 这个社区地理位置优越，处于东西欧之间的战略要地。

sentences.en: Merchants traveling across the region would sometimes pass through Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 穿梭于该地区的商人们有时会路过华沙。

sentences.en: During the Middle Ages, it gradually became an important town.
sentences.zh: 在中世纪时期，它逐渐发展成了一个重要的城镇。

sentences.en: The population increased, and the settlement grew.
sentences.zh: 人口增加，定居点也不断扩大。

sentences.en: Although cities like Krakow were far more powerful and far more influential, Warsaw was beginning to establish itself as an important place.
sentences.zh: 尽管像克拉科夫这样的城市曾经更具权势和影响力，但华沙开始确立其重要地位。

sentences.en: Today, we think of roads or railways as the main ways to transport people and goods.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们认为公路或铁路是运输人员和货物的主要方式。

sentences.en: But during the Middle Ages, rivers were the equivalent of highways.
sentences.zh: 但在中世纪，河流就相当于高速公路。

sentences.en: If you could travel by water, it was much faster and much more efficient, especially as most of the continent, most of Europe, was covered by forests and didn’t have nice roads or paths to go between different cities.
sentences.zh: 如果你能走水路，速度会快得多，效率也高得多，特别是当时整个欧洲大陆大部分都被森林覆盖，并没有连接不同城市的良好道路或小径。

sentences.en: Cities located next to major rivers were often the cities that became wealthy and politically important.
sentences.zh: 毗邻主要河流的城市往往能变得富有并在政治上占据重要地位。

sentences.en: Merchants used rivers to transport food, wood, salt, cloth, any other products between different parts of the continent.
sentences.zh: 商人们利用河流在欧洲大陆的不同地区之间运输食物、木材、盐、布料以及各种其他产品。

sentences.en: You’ll know this if you’ve listened to my previous episodes on the history of various cities.
sentences.zh: 如果你听过我先前关于各大城市历史的节目，你就会知道这一点。

sentences.en: New York, London, Istanbul, Rome, Berlin, Nagasaki, all of these places are built on important rivers or important coastlines.
sentences.zh: 纽约、伦敦、伊斯坦布尔、罗马、柏林、长崎，所有这些地方都建立在重要的河流或重要的海岸线上。

sentences.en: Warsaw’s location on a river was therefore very important.
sentences.zh: 因此，华沙濒临河流的地理位置非常重要。

sentences.en: And like many old European cities, Warsaw has some fascinating legends and folklore about its name’s history.
sentences.zh: 和许多欧洲古城一样，华沙也有一些关于其名字由来的迷人传说和民间故事。

sentences.en: One famous story explains the origin of the city’s name through two characters called Wars and Sawa.
sentences.zh: 一个著名的故事通过两个名叫 Wars 和 Sawa 的人物解释了这座城市名字的由来。

sentences.en: I think that’s how you pronounce them. In some versions of the story, Wars was a fisherman and Sawa was a mermaid.
sentences.zh: 我想他们是这么发音的。在故事的一些版本中，Wars 是一个渔民，而 Sawa 是一位人鱼。

sentences.en: In others, they were a normal couple who welcomed a traveling prince.
sentences.zh: 在另一些版本中，他们是一对接待了一位旅行王子的普通夫妇。

sentences.en: Over time, their names were supposed to combine to create Warszawa, which is kind of like the Polish name for Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他们的名字被认为组合成了 Warszawa，这有点像是波兰语中华沙的名字。

sentences.en: Sorry, I’ve mispronounced it probably. Another famous symbol in the city is the Warsaw mermaid.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我可能发音不准。城中的另一个著名标志是华沙人鱼。

sentences.en: Statues of the mermaid can be found throughout the city.
sentences.zh: 人鱼的雕像在全城各地随处可见。

sentences.en: And according to legend, the mermaid was supposed to protect the people of Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 根据传说，人鱼理应保护华沙的人民。

sentences.en: Stories like this give us a chance right now to talk about myths, legends, and folklore.
sentences.zh: 像这样的故事正好让我们有机会聊聊神话、传说和民间故事。

sentences.en: A myth is usually a traditional story involving gods or supernatural explanations of the world.
sentences.zh: 神话通常是涉及神灵或对世界做出超自然解释的传统故事。

sentences.en: A legend is typically connected to real places and historical figures, although parts of the story might not be true.
sentences.zh: 传说通常与真实的地方和历史人物相关，尽管故事的部分内容可能并非事实。

sentences.en: And folklore is a broader term that includes stories, customs, beliefs, and traditions held by people.
sentences.zh: 而民间故事则是一个更广泛的概念，包括人们所持有的故事、习俗、信仰和传统。

sentences.en: As I said before, Warsaw wasn’t always the capital of Poland.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，华沙并非一直都是波兰的首都。

sentences.en: For a long time, that was Kraków. Kraków is a southern city that was the royal capital of the Polish kingdom.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，首都都是克拉科夫。克拉科夫是南部的一座城市，曾是波兰王国的皇家首都。

sentences.en: Polish kings were crowned there, and it was considered one of the most important cities in Central Europe.
sentences.zh: 波兰国王在那里加冕，它被视为中欧最重要的城市之一。

sentences.en: In the late 1500s, the king decided to transfer the royal court from Kraków to Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 在 16 世纪末，国王决定将王廷从克拉科夫迁往华沙。

sentences.en: The move was completed in the beginning of the 17th century, around the year 1611.
sentences.zh: 这次迁都于 17 世纪初完成，大约在 1611 年左右。

sentences.en: Technically, though, Warsaw didn’t officially become the named capital until later, but it was functionally the capital once the king moved there.
sentences.zh: 不过严格来说，华沙直到后来才正式获得首都之名，但自从国王搬到那里后，它在功能上就已经成了首都。

sentences.en: Warsaw was located more centrally within the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.
sentences.zh: 华沙在波兰立陶宛联邦内处于更靠中央的位置。

sentences.en: This was an enormous political union that connected the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.
sentences.zh: 这是一个庞大的政治联盟，连接了波兰王国和立陶宛大公国。

sentences.en: At its height, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth was one of the largest and most powerful states in all of Europe.
sentences.zh: 在其鼎盛时期，波兰立陶宛联邦是整个欧洲最大、最强大的国家之一。

sentences.en: It included parts of Poland, Lithuania, Belarus, Latvia, and Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 它包括波兰、立陶宛、白俄罗斯、拉脱维亚和乌克兰的部分地区。

sentences.en: Because the state was so large, governing it from Kraków in the far south was a bit inconvenient.
sentences.zh: 由于国家版图如此之大，从极南端的克拉科夫对其进行统治多少有些不便。

sentences.en: Warsaw’s more central location made ruling the Commonwealth a bit easier.
sentences.zh: 华沙更居中的地理位置使得统治该联邦变得容易了一些。

sentences.en: Warsaw is also between the cities of Kraków and Vilnius.
sentences.zh: 华沙也恰好在克拉科夫和维尔纽斯两座城市之间。

sentences.en: Vilnius is the historical capital of Lithuania, so choosing Warsaw as the capital meant that it was kind of in the middle, a compromise.
sentences.zh: 维尔纽斯是立陶宛的历史首都，因此选择华沙作为首都意味着它大致处于中间位置，是一种折中方案。

sentences.en: The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth was an unusual political system for its time.
sentences.zh: 波兰立陶宛联邦在其时代是一个不同寻常的政治体制。

sentences.en: Unlike many European countries which were ruled by strong, absolute monarchs or strong kings and strong queens, the Commonwealth gave most of its power to the nobility.
sentences.zh: 与许多由强有力、专制的君主或强势国王与女王统治的欧洲国家不同，该联邦将大部分权力赋予了贵族。

sentences.en: Kings were elected rather than automatically inheriting power, and the important decisions made in the Commonwealth often required approval from a kind of parliament.
sentences.zh: 国王是通过选举产生，而不是自动世袭权力，而且联邦做出的重大决定通常需要得到某种议会的批准。

sentences.en: Of course, it was not a democratic system by what we now understand as democracy, but compared to many other European countries at the time, the Commonwealth was considered relatively open especially for noble people.
sentences.zh: 当然，以我们今天对民主的理解来看，它并不是一个民主制度，但与当时许多其他欧洲国家相比，该联邦被认为相对开放，尤其是对贵族而言。

sentences.en: It was also very multicultural and multiethnic.
sentences.zh: 它也非常具有多元文化和多民族特点。

sentences.en: Poles, Lithuanians, Jews, Ukrainians, Germans, Armenians, and many other communities lived inside the Commonwealth.
sentences.zh: 波兰人、立陶宛人、犹太人、乌克兰人、德国人、亚美尼亚人以及许多其他群体都生活在联邦境内。

sentences.en: This meant there were multiple languages, religions, and traditions.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这里存在多种语言、宗教和传统。

sentences.en: Warsaw became the capital of this enormous state.
sentences.zh: 华沙成为了这个庞大帝国的首都。

sentences.en: The population grew. Wealthy nobles built grand palaces and elegant residences in Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 人口增长了。富有的贵族们在华沙建造了宏伟的宫殿和优雅的宅邸。

sentences.en: And the city hosted royal ceremonies, diplomatic events if other countries’ leaders came to visit.
sentences.zh: 这座城市还举办了皇家典礼，以及其他国家领导人来访时的外交活动。

sentences.en: Gradually though, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth became weaker, especially during the 1700s.
sentences.zh: 不过渐渐地，波兰立陶宛联邦开始走向衰落，尤其是在 18 世纪期间。

sentences.en: At the same time, nearby countries like Russia and Prussia and Austria were becoming more and more powerful, and more and more ambitious.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，周边的俄罗斯、普鲁士和奥地利等国正变得越来越强大，野心也越来越大。

sentences.en: Eventually, these countries decided to divide Poland among themselves.
sentences.zh: 最终，这些国家决定瓜分波兰。

sentences.en: In a series of events known as the Partitions of Poland, the territory of the Commonwealth was gradually split between Russia, Prussia, and Austria.
sentences.zh: 在一系列被称为“瓜分波兰”的事件中，联邦的领土逐渐被俄罗斯、普鲁士和奥地利瓜分。

sentences.en: There were three separate partitions in 1772, 1793, and 1795.
sentences.zh: 分别在 1772 年、1793 年和 1795 年进行了三次瓜分。

sentences.en: After the final partition, Poland disappeared.
sentences.zh: 在最后一次瓜分后，波兰消失了。

sentences.en: Poland completely disappeared from the map of Europe.
sentences.zh: 波兰彻底从欧洲地图上消失了。

sentences.en: For more than 100 years, there was no independent Poland.
sentences.zh: 在 100 多年的时间里，没有独立的波兰。

sentences.en: No Polish state. This is one of the most fascinating, extraordinary parts of Polish history.
sentences.zh: 没有波兰国。这是波兰历史上最迷人、最非凡的部分之一。

sentences.en: Imagine your country suddenly no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 想象一下你的国家突然不复存在了。

sentences.en: It no longer has a place on the map of the world.
sentences.zh: 它在世界地图上不再有一席之地。

sentences.en: Well, this happened to Poland. Warsaw eventually ended up in the Russian Empire.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就在波兰身上发生了。华沙最终落入了俄罗斯帝国的手中。

sentences.en: The Russian Empire ruled a lot of central and eastern Poland during the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 19 世纪期间，俄罗斯帝国统治了波兰中部和东部的广大地区。

sentences.en: Many Polish people strongly opposed Russian rule, and different uprisings broke out against Russian authorities.
sentences.zh: 许多波兰人强烈反对俄国统治，针对俄国当局爆发了多次起义。

sentences.en: Two of the most famous rebellions were the November Uprising of 1830 and the January Uprising of 1863.
sentences.zh: 其中最著名的两次叛乱是 1830 年的十一月起义和 1863 年的一月起义。

sentences.en: Both of these were ultimately unsuccessful.
sentences.zh: 这两次起义最终都失败了。

sentences.en: The Russian Empire responded harshly. They attempted to suppress, to stop, Polish nationalism and Polish resistance movements.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯帝国做出了严厉的回应。他们试图镇压、遏制波兰的民族主义和波兰的抵抗运动。

sentences.en: They did this by using severe punishments and restricting political freedoms.
sentences.zh: 他们通过严厉惩罚和限制政治自由来达到这一目的。

sentences.en: For example, they limited the use of Polish language in schools and some government institutions.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们限制了波兰语在学校和一些政府机构中的使用。

sentences.en: But despite this, Polish identity survived.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，波兰人的身份认同依然得以存续。

sentences.en: Polish people worked hard to keep their culture, and Warsaw was a big part of this Polish identity.​ After more than 100 years of foreign occupation, Poland finally regained independence at the end of World War I.
sentences.zh: 波兰人民努力守护他们的文化，而华沙正是这种波兰身份认同的重要部分。在经历了 100 多年的外国占领后，波兰终于在第一次世界大战结束时重获独立。

sentences.en: This new period of independence was known as the Second Polish Republic, and Warsaw officially became the capital of this new republic.
sentences.zh: 这段新的独立时期被称为波兰第二共和国，而华沙正式成为这个新共和国的首都。

sentences.en: The interwar period, which means the years between World War I and World War II, was a time of optimism in.
sentences.zh: 两次世界大战之间的时期，也就是一战和二战之间的年份，是充满乐观情绪的时期。

sentences.en: It was also a difficult time. There was enormous excitement about rebuilding the country, but so many challenges.
sentences.zh: 这也是一段艰难的时期。人们对重建国家充满了巨大的兴奋，但也伴随着诸多的挑战。

sentences.en: Poland had to unite parts of the country that had been controlled by different empires for more than a century.
sentences.zh: 波兰必须将那些被不同帝国控制了 一个多世纪的国家部分统一起来。

sentences.en: The economy was unstable, and there was political arguments quite often.
sentences.zh: 经济不稳定，政治争论也相当频繁。

sentences.en: Also, the country faced tensions with some of the neighboring countries.
sentences.zh: 此外，该国还面临着与一些邻国的紧张关系。

sentences.en: And then, in September 1939, Germany invaded Poland.
sentences.zh: 接着，在 1939 年 9 月，德国入侵了波兰。

sentences.en: The invasion happened with shocking speed and violence.
sentences.zh: 这场入侵以令人震惊的速度和暴力展开。

sentences.en: German forces attacked from the west. They used tanks, aircraft, and rapid military movement to quickly invade Poland.
sentences.zh: 德军从西部发动进攻。他们使用坦克、飞机和迅猛的军事调动迅速入侵了波兰。

sentences.en: Warsaw became one of the main targets for the German attacks.
sentences.zh: 华沙成为了德国袭击的主要目标之一。

sentences.en: Within days, the city had been heavily bombed from the air.
sentences.zh: 几天之内，这座城市就遭到了猛烈的空袭。

sentences.en: Buildings collapsed. Fires spread throughout the neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 建筑物倒塌。大火在各街区蔓延。

sentences.en: Thousands of people were killed or injured.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人死伤。

sentences.en: Polish soldiers and normal people resisted, but Warsaw was surrounded by German forces.
sentences.zh: 波兰士兵和普通民众进行了抵抗，但华沙被德军包围了。

sentences.en: This period became known as the Siege of Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 这一时期被称为华沙围城战。

sentences.en: For several weeks, the city continued fighting under constant attacks, but they started to run out of food, and the city was becoming more and more damaged.
sentences.zh: 在长达数周的时间里，这座城市在不断的袭击中坚持战斗，但他们的食物开始耗尽，城市受到的破坏也越来越严重。

sentences.en: Eventually, the Germans captured Warsaw at the end of September 1939.
sentences.zh: 最终，德军于 1939 年 9 月底攻占了华沙。

sentences.en: Under Nazi occupation, Warsaw became the site of some of the worst atrocities of the war.
sentences.zh: 在纳粹占领下，华沙成为了这场战争中最惨绝人寰的暴行发生地之一。

sentences.en: In 1940, the Nazis ordered Jewish residents of Warsaw to move into a sealed part of the city, which had been surrounded by walls and guarded checkpoints.
sentences.zh: 1940 年，纳粹下令将华沙的犹太居民赶进城市中一个封闭的区域，四周建起了高墙并设有戒备森严的检查站。

sentences.en: This was known as the Warsaw Ghetto. More than 400,000 Jewish people were forced into an extremely overcrowded area with terrible living conditions.
sentences.zh: 这就是著名的华沙犹太人区。超过 40 万犹太人被迫挤在一个极端拥挤、生活条件极其恶劣的地区。

sentences.en: Families separated, people starving, diseases spreading through the area.
sentences.zh: 家庭离散，人们忍饥挨饿，疾病在区内蔓延。

sentences.en: Beginning in 1942, hundreds of thousands of Jewish residents were transported from the ghetto to Nazi death camps.
sentences.zh: 从 1942 年开始，成百上千的犹太居民被从犹太人区运送到纳粹的死亡集中营。

sentences.en: Most were murdered shortly after they arrived as part of the Holocaust.
sentences.zh: 作为大屠杀的一部分，大多数人在抵达后不久就被谋杀了。

sentences.en: Yet, even in these conditions, people resisted.
sentences.zh: 然而，即便在这样的环境下，人们仍在抵抗。

sentences.en: In 1943, Jewish fighters inside the ghetto launched what became known as the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising.
sentences.zh: 1943 年，犹太人区内的抵抗战士发起了后来被称为华沙犹太人区起义的行动。

sentences.en: They had no chance of victory. They had no weapons, and they were up against much stronger German military, but they chose to resist.
sentences.zh: 他们没有任何获胜的可能。他们没有武器，面对的是强大得多的德军，但他们选择了抵抗。

sentences.en: They chose to fight, instead of just accepting their deaths and deportation.
sentences.zh: 他们选择去战斗，而不是仅仅接受死亡和被流放的命运。

sentences.en: For nearly a month, the fighters held out against German forces.
sentences.zh: 抵抗战士们与德军坚持对抗了近一个月。

sentences.en: Eventually, the uprising was crushed, and much of the ghetto destroyed.​ In 1944, another major uprising began, the Warsaw Uprising.
sentences.zh: 最终，起义被残酷镇压，犹太人区的大部分地区也被摧毁。在 1944 年，另一场重大起义爆发了，即华沙起义。

sentences.en: This uprising was organized mainly by the Polish resistance movement, known as the Home Army.
sentences.zh: 这场起义主要是由被称为“家乡军”的波兰抵抗运动组织起来的。

sentences.en: Their goal was to save Warsaw from German occupation before Soviet forces entered the city.
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是在苏联军队进入城市之前，将华沙从德国占领中解放出来。

sentences.en: They hoped that they could regain control of Warsaw and demonstrate that Poland could be an independent country after the war.
sentences.zh: 他们希望能够重新掌控华沙，并证明波兰在战后能够成为一个独立的国家。

sentences.en: On August 1st, 1944, thousands of resistance fighters launched attacks across the city.
sentences.zh: 1944 年 8 月 1 日，数千名抵抗战士在全城各地发动了袭击。

sentences.en: Ordinary people built barricades and supported resistance fighters, but they lacked weapons and they lacked supplies, and Germany responded with overwhelming violence, overwhelming brutality.
sentences.zh: 普通百姓筑起街垒并支援抵抗战士，但他们缺乏武器和物资，而德国则以排山倒海般的暴力和残酷进行了回击。

sentences.en: Fighting consumed the city for 63 days. Meanwhile, Soviet forces had arrived in the area.
sentences.zh: 战火在这座城市持续燃烧了 63 天。与此同时，苏军已经抵达该地区。

sentences.en: They remained across the river and did not intervene in time.
sentences.zh: 他们驻扎在河对岸，并未及时施以援手。

sentences.en: Historians still debate today why the Soviet Army didn’t help the people of Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 时至今日，历史学家仍在争论苏军当年为何不肯帮助华沙人民。

sentences.en: For many Polish people today, the lack of Soviet assistance during World War II is a painful part of the war.
sentences.zh: 对于今天许多波兰人来说，二战期间苏联的袖手旁观是战争中一段痛苦的记忆。

sentences.en: Eventually, the uprising failed. It collapsed.
sentences.zh: 最终，起义失败了。它崩塌了。

sentences.en: After defeating the resistance the German army carried out a near total destruction of Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 在击溃抵抗力量后，德军对华沙实施了近乎彻底的毁灭。

sentences.en: They destroyed everything. Historical buildings, homes, libraries, churches, they were all intentionally demolished.
sentences.zh: 他们摧毁了一切。历史建筑、家园、图书馆、教堂，全都被蓄意拆毁。

sentences.en: By the end of the war, around 85% of Warsaw had been destroyed.
sentences.zh: 到战争结束时，大约 85% 的华沙已被摧毁。

sentences.en: It had been almost completely erased. When the war ended in 1945, Warsaw barely existed.
sentences.zh: 它几乎被完全从地面上抹去了。当 1945 年战争结束时，华沙已经不复存在。

sentences.en: It barely existed as a functioning city.
sentences.zh: 它作为一座正常运转的城市几乎不复存在了。

sentences.en: At the same time, Poland entered a completely new era.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，波兰进入了一个全新的时代。

sentences.en: Although the war was over, Poland did not become independent in the way that people had hoped.
sentences.zh: 尽管战争已经结束，但波兰并没有像人们所希望的那样获得独立。

sentences.en: Instead, the country fell under Soviet influence and gradually became a communist state aligned with the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 相反，该国陷入了苏联的势力范围，并逐渐沦为一个紧跟苏联的共产主义国家。

sentences.en: A new communist regime took power, and they were supported politically and militarily by Moscow.
sentences.zh: 一个新的共产主义政权上台了，他们在政治和军事上得到了莫斯科的支持。

sentences.en: Under this system, Poland had to rebuild, and especially they had to rebuild Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 在这种体制下，波兰必须进行重建，特别是他们必须重建华沙。

sentences.en: In some places, this meant rebuilding entire new districts.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，这意味着要重建全新的一整片区域。

sentences.en: In other areas, especially in the historical center, they tried to recreate the old districts, recreate the old city, as accurately as possible.
sentences.zh: 而在其他地方，特别是在历史中心区，他们试图尽可能准确地重现旧日的街区、重现旧城。

sentences.en: They carefully rebuilt many of Warsaw’s historic streets.
sentences.zh: 他们精心重建了华沙的许多历史街道。

sentences.en: One especially important source of information to help them base their designs on were the detailed paintings of an 18th-century artist called Bernardo Bellotto.
sentences.zh: 为他们的设计提供依据的一个极其重要的信息来源，是 18 世纪艺术家博尔纳多·贝洛托的细致画作。

sentences.en: His artworks captured the appearance of Warsaw before it was destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他的艺术作品捕捉了华沙被毁前的面貌。

sentences.en: Today, if you go to Warsaw and you walk around Old Town, it feels like you’re surrounded by medieval or early modern architecture.
sentences.zh: 今天，如果你去华沙并在老城区漫步，你会感觉自己仿佛置身于中世纪或近代早期的建筑群中。

sentences.en: But actually, what you’re seeing was almost entirely rebuilt after 1945.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你所看到的几乎全部都是在 1945 年之后重建的。

sentences.en: The reconstruction was so remarkable that UNESCO recognized Warsaw Old Town as an outstanding example of near total historical reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 这次重建如此非凡，以至于联合国教科文组织将华沙老城区认定为几近完全的历史复原的杰出范例。

sentences.en: But of course, Warsaw’s post-war identity, Warsaw’s story, was deeply influenced by communist politics.
sentences.zh: 但当然，华沙战后的身份认同、华沙的故事，深受共产主义政治的影响。

sentences.en: On the one side, Warsaw had lots of reconstructed churches and historical squares and streets.
sentences.zh: 一方面，华沙拥有大量重建的教堂、历史广场和街道。

sentences.en: But on the other side, there were massive socialist buildings.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，这里耸立着庞大的社会主义建筑。

sentences.en: Those big apartment blocks and socialist architecture designed to symbolize communist power and communist modernization.
sentences.zh: 那些大型公寓楼和社会主义建筑旨在象征共产主义的力量与现代化。

sentences.en: The Palace of Culture and Science is an example.
sentences.zh: 文化科学宫便是一个例子。

sentences.en: It was completed in the 1950s, and a gift from the Soviet Union to the Polish people.
sentences.zh: 它于 20 世纪 50 年代完工，是苏联送给波兰人民的礼物。

sentences.en: The building dominated Warsaw’s skyline, but it has always been controversial.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑主导了华沙的天际线，但它一直备受争议。

sentences.en: Life in communist Poland was complex. The country was rebuilt and industry expanded, but freedom was heavily, heavily restricted.
sentences.zh: 共产主义时期的波兰生活复杂多变。国家得到了重建，工业也得以扩张，但自由受到了极其严厉的限制。

sentences.en: The communist government-controlled media, closely monitored public life.
sentences.zh: 共产主义政府控制着媒体，对公众生活进行密切监控。

sentences.en: There were also economic problems becoming quite serious in the 1970s and’80s.
sentences.zh: 到了 20 世纪 70 和 80 年代，经济问题也变得相当严重。

sentences.en: Resistance to communism grew across Poland.
sentences.zh: 全波兰反对共产主义的抵抗情绪日益高涨。

sentences.en: One of the most important developments was the rise of the Solidarity movement in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 其中最重要的发展之一便是 20 世纪 80 年代“团结工会”运动的兴起。

sentences.en: Solidarity was originally an independent trade union formed in the shipyards of Gdansk, and it quickly became a massive social and political movement, demanding workers’ rights, reforms, and greater political freedom.
sentences.zh: 团结工会最初是格但斯克造船厂成立的一个独立工会，它迅速演变成一场庞大的社会和政治运动，要求工人权利、改革和更大的政治自由。

sentences.en: By the late 1980s, communist governments across Eastern Europe were becoming weaker.
sentences.zh: 到了 20 世纪 80 年代末，东欧各国的共产主义政府日渐式微。

sentences.en: The Soviet Union was struggling, economically and politically, and there was this new pressure for reform.
sentences.zh: 苏联在经济和政治上举步维艰，改革的呼声不断高涨。

sentences.en: In 1989, Poland held partially free elections.
sentences.zh: 1989 年，波兰举行了部分自由选举。

sentences.en: This was the beginning of the end of communist rule.
sentences.zh: 这是共产主义统治走向终结的开始。

sentences.en: Poland was one of the first countries in the Eastern Bloc, the countries influenced by the Soviet Union, to move away from communism peacefully.
sentences.zh: 波兰是东欧集团（受苏联影响的国家）中最早和平摆脱共产主义的国家之一。

sentences.en: Today, Warsaw is one of the fastest-growing cities in Central Europe.
sentences.zh: 如今，华沙是中欧发展最快的城市之一。

sentences.en: Global corporations have opened offices in Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 全球跨国公司纷纷在华沙设立办公室。

sentences.en: There are cafes and museums, tall skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 那里有咖啡馆、博物馆和高耸的摩天大楼。

sentences.en: The city now attracts international students and international workers.
sentences.zh: 这座城市现在吸引着国际学生和外籍员工。

sentences.en: Tourism has grown as people have become more interested in Poland.
sentences.zh: 随着人们对波兰的兴趣日益浓厚，旅游业也随之发展壮大。

sentences.en: In fact, I could do an entire episode, I might do an entire episode, on the rise of Poland.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我可以出一期节目，我可能也会出一期节目，专门讲讲波兰的崛起。

sentences.en: Poland is one of the success stories of countries that used to be aligned with the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 波兰是那些曾经紧跟苏联的国家中成功的典范之一。

sentences.en: I think what makes Warsaw fascinating is that it has this mixture of histories.
sentences.zh: 我认为华沙最迷人的地方在于它融合了多种历史。

sentences.en: There are carefully rebuilt historical sites from the medieval period, and then communist-era massive apartment buildings which represent life between 1945 and 1990, and then the modern skyscrapers that exist today.
sentences.zh: 这里既有从中世纪精心重建的历史古迹，又有代表 1945 年至 1990 年间生活的共产主义时期巨型公寓楼，还有当今存在的现代摩天大楼。

sentences.en: Warsaw also represents something more. Warsaw was occupied, divided, almost completely destroyed, rebuilt under communism, and now modernizing again after the end of the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 华沙还代表着更深层的意义。华沙曾被占领、被瓜分、几乎彻底被毁，在共产主义下重建，而现在在冷战结束后又再次实现现代化。

sentences.en: Warsaw’s history is one of the most interesting stories in Europe.
sentences.zh: 华沙的历史是欧洲最有趣的故事之一。

sentences.en: It has survived foreign occupation, disappeared politically for more than a century, experienced the horrors of World War II, and was almost completely destroyed.
sentences.zh: 它在外国占领下幸存，在政治上消失了一个多世纪，经历了第二次世界大战的恐怖，并且几乎被完全摧毁。

sentences.en: But it rebuilt itself, and now the city is modern, international, and in Poland.
sentences.zh: 但它完成了自我重建，如今这座城市既现代、国际化，又深植于波兰。

sentences.en: Poland is one of the most exciting and quickly growing countries in Europe.
sentences.zh: 波兰是欧洲最令人兴奋且发展最快的国家之一。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Have you visited Warsaw?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你参观过华沙吗？

sentences.en: Would you like to visit? How should cities remember traumatic events like war and occupation?
sentences.zh: 你想去参观吗？城市应该如何铭记战争和占领等创伤性事件？

sentences.en: And what city should I cover next in this series?
sentences.zh: 在这个系列中，我接下来应该讲哪座城市？
